page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 40 virtual CPUs derived from 20 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz and features a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding 4.8 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple tests. In raw compute, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 2133.36 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, with write speeds at 48.09 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 25.35 GB/sec and processed 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second. Large language model inference speeds reached 1841.39 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, but dropped to 56.94 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed of 3.1 GHz provide a stable, predictable resource profile for compute-heavy tasks without the overhead of bundled storage or GPU accelerators. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider. This hardware configuration is suited for workloads such as database operations, software compilation, web serving, and moderate-scale data processing tasks that benefit from dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon cores and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio.
